text:
lina: heads up 1h ago ran the orca-lite-int8 NDJSON canary and saw a jump in parse failures. looks like the model is emitting JSON inside markdown code fences sometimes which breaks our NDJSON stream parser. sample below.
tom: paste raw example?
lina: raw snippet from the response stream (note triple backticks + following NDJSON object):
```
```json
{"tool":"enrich","args":{"id":"acct_987","meta":{"tags":["onboard","trial"]}}}
```

{"tool":"log_event","args":{"type":"onboard","status":"ok"}}
```

devbot: Canary run 1797654200: schema_fail_rate=0.42% (baseline=0.11%), parse_err_count=212, affected_variants=[orca-lite-int8], streaming_mode=ndjson
ops-ci: interesting. our NDJSON parser expects one JSON object per newline and no fences. code fences introduce extra newlines and backticks so the stream reader tries to parse the fence or the inner braces at mismatched boundaries.
mike: quick question: is the inner JSON well-formed? it looks valid but wrapped in fences, so parser sees a line of backticks then the object then backticks then another object -> it tries to parse backticks as JSON and fails.
lina: exactly. heuristics: about 80% of these events are code-fence-wrapped, 15% are triple-quoted strings where model included additional explanation lines after the JSON, 5% are actual truncations.
tom: short-term mitigation ideas?
ops-ci: two pragmatic short-term fixes: 1) pre-parse sanitizer that strips leading/trailing fenced code blocks before NDJSON parsing (only if the fence contains valid JSON inside) 2) a fallback that scans for the first JSON object in a buffer using a cheap brace-counter and parses that. both are applied only in canary.
mike: sanitizer risks: if model intentionally included text after the JSON we might drop important context. but for tool-calling we only care about the JSON object, so acceptable for canary. still add golden-set validator to avoid accepting wrong keys.
lina: implemented a conservative sanitizer in the canary (strip only ```json fences and fenced blocks where the inner text starts with '{' and passes a quick JSON validity check). result: schema_fail_rate dropped 0.42% -> 0.15% but we observed 0.03% accidental data-loss (cases where the model appended a human clarifying sentence after JSON that we trimmed). logged examples to s3://redwood-canaries/ndjson/1797654200/fence-trim-examples.ndjson
tom: mid-term approach: length-prefixed JSON. have the model emit a single token-length prefix like `<JSON_LEN=NNN>` on its own line before the JSON. parser reads NNN bytes and interprets that slice as one JSON object, ignoring fences. safer across streaming boundaries.
ops-ci: agree. but must ensure sentinel token is tokenizer-safe and not splittable. propose using a closed-vocab sentinel chosen from tokenizer-safe set, e.g. `</s>__JL__LEN=` followed by digits and newline. we'll run a tokenizer collision scan.
